note: Small loop along Spring Creek, 2 mi up Spring Creek Rd (FR 744) off Taylor Canyon Rd (CR 742), near the Taylor River's gold-medal water and the Fossil Ridge Wilderness, ~8,500 ft. ~35 ft max RV (not for big rigs, but fine for a 23-ft rig). --Claude
summary: FS page + recreation.gov: confirmed 12 sites, FCFS only (Scan and Pay), $18 (+$9 extra vehicle), no electric, no water, vault toilets. Added potable_water false, season (late spring - early fall), fees checked 2026. No length on any agency page (the '~35 ft' is unsourced). Dump (derived from the old note) left; FS page silent. Note cleaned.
flags: Phone missing: Gunnison Ranger District 970-641-0471 (the GMUG conditions page: 'contact the Gunnison Ranger District front office for road condition updates at 970-641-0471'). The campground page itself has no contact block; recreation.gov lists no phone.

Length: neither the FS page nor recreation.gov (one placeholder Scan and Pay site, no attributes) gives any length; the stored note's '~35 ft max RV (not for big rigs...)' has no agency source. The agency is silent rather than singling the campground out, so no criteria problem.

Road: the FS page gives only directions ('travel 7.25 miles [on CR 742 to] Forest Road 744. Turn left FDR 744 (Spring Creek Road) and drive 2 miles'), no surface or RV wording; GMUG's conditions page says to call the Gunnison RD for road conditions. No closure order found for the area (the only GMUG alert, Gold Mountain fire, is on the Ouray RD).
Facilities: stored dump: true (derived from the old note 'dump available') has no support on the FS page or recreation.gov; left as derived, but it looks doubtful for a 12-site no-water campground.

Waterfront (stored creekside, confirmed): on imagery Spring Creek (~5-10 m wide) runs down the east side of the loop; the east-side sites at the north end are ~30-45 m from it across open meadow with no road or buffer. A creek under ~30 m is creekside by size.
Pin: stored 38.74803,-106.76709 = recreation.gov/FS point, at the loop's south entrance; the loop runs ~150 m north of it. Within 500 m.
